judgments.label: false_positive
judgments.rationale: Offscreen skip link 'Skip to navigation' with href="#navigation". In the snapshot the id 'navigation' is on the first link of the main navigation (the 'News' pillar link), so the link does move the user to the site navigation, exactly as its text says. The model took the name of the target element ('News') for the link's destination; landing on the first nav item is what skipping to navigation means. The link text describes its purpose; no 2.4.4 failure.

judgments.label: false_positive
judgments.rationale: Header sub-navigation link 'UK' (href /uk-news, destination title 'Latest UK news | The Guardian') inside a nav list of news sections: World, US politics, UK, Climate crisis, Middle East, Ukraine, Environment... On a news site's section navigation, a link named 'UK' among other section names clearly leads to the UK news section, and the destination confirms it. The purpose is determinable from the link text in its programmatically determined context (the navigation list); 'nothing around it does' is wrong. Not a 2.4.4 failure.

judgments.label: false_positive
judgments.rationale: 'Learn more' link (to /info/2024/feb/28/what-is-the-deeply-read-list) sits directly under the h3 'Deeply read', inside the sentence 'What readers are spending time with (Learn more)'. The enclosing sentence (G53) and the immediately preceding heading (H80) make the purpose clear: learn more about the Deeply read list. Its context is programmatically determined, so 2.4.4 is met; the claim that nothing around it explains it is wrong. (It would fail 2.4.9 AAA, which is not the criterion named.)

judgments.label: uncertain
judgments.rationale: The element is the masthead edition picker: a visually clipped checkbox (tabindex=-1) labelled by a visible <label> 'Int' that toggles a hidden list of edition links (International, UK, US, Australia, Europe edition); the live HTML is the same. The finding's framing is off: it is a disclosure toggle, nothing is 'entered', and the patch ('Include in masthead') shows the model misread the control. Read fairly, though, the claim is that 'Int' does not describe the control's purpose, and that is arguable: 'Int' is a cryptic abbreviation of the current edition and says nothing about choosing an edition, so a screen reader hears 'Int, checkbox, not checked'. Others would pass it as the established visual edition-switcher pattern and file the real problems under 4.1.2 (checkbox role for a menu button) and 2.1.1. Competent auditors would disagree on the 2.4.6 call.

judgments.label: uncertain
judgments.rationale: The h3 card headline 'Henry Harris' recipe for tarte Vaudoise à la creme' (Food section) has no lang markup, so the French dish name is read with English rules. 3.1.2 exempts proper names and words that have become part of the surrounding vernacular. 'Tarte vaudoise à la crème' is not English vernacular, and a strict auditor would ask for lang="fr" on the multi-word French phrase. Many others treat a dish's name in an English recipe headline as a name, which needs no language change, and the passage is short and still understandable. The evidence does not settle which reading applies; competent auditors would reasonably disagree.
